A.explanation: Point A is at the free surface of the 30 cm column, so depth $h = 0$ and gauge pressure $\rho g h = 0$.

B.explanation: Point B is about $20 \text{ cm}$ below the surface, the largest depth of the four positions, so $p = \rho g h$ is greatest.

C.explanation: Point C is at the free surface of the 10 cm column, so depth $h = 0$ and gauge pressure is zero.

D.explanation: Point D is at the base of the 10 cm column, so $h = 10 \text{ cm}$, which is less than the depth of B.

hints: Notice whether each marked point is at the liquid surface or below it - pressure depends on depth below the surface, not total height of the cylinder.
Recall $p = \rho g h$ for the same liquid, so compare the vertical distance $h$ from the surface down to A, B, C and D.
Use the dashed line joining B to the surface at C to find the depth of B, then compare it with the $10 \text{ cm}$ depth of D.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: for the same liquid, gauge pressure at a point is $p = \rho g h$, where $h$ is the depth measured down from the free surface.
Point A is on the surface of the left 30 cm column, so $h_A = 0$. Point C is on the surface of the 10 cm column, so $h_C = 0$.
Point D is at the base of the right 10 cm column, so $h_D = 10 \text{ cm}$.

Point B is inside the second 30 cm column at the same horizontal level as the surface C, which is $10 \text{ cm}$ above the base. So its depth is $h_B = 30 \text{ cm} - 10 \text{ cm} = 20 \text{ cm}$.
Compare depths: $h_B = 20 \text{ cm} > h_D = 10 \text{ cm} > h_A = h_C = 0$. Since $\rho$ and $g$ are the same, the largest $h$ gives the largest $p$.
Therefore the pressure is greatest at B. This is option B.
